newsitem.title: THAILAND: Banks cheap in depressed Thai market - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Banks cheap in depressed Thai market - analysts.

text.p: Analysts urged investors on Tuesday to pick up discounted Thai bank blue-chips, saying they are a sound long-term investment after an extended bear move on the Thai bourse.
Thanadee Soponsiri, chairman of Nava Finance and Securities Plc, said major Thai banks currently carry a 10-11 percent price/earnings ratio against a 15 average for the whole battered market.

"Thai banking is a sound industry traditionally growing along with the economy. Efficiently run banks would not do badly in an economy that expands nearly eight percent a year," Thanadee told an equity market seminar.
He favoured Thailand's top three banks -- Bangkok Bank Plc, Thai Farmers Bank Plc and the Siam Commercial Bank Plc.

Kongkiat Opaswongse, chairman of Assets Plus Co, said he expects the Thai bank sector to post about 10 percent earnings growth this year while many other sectors would likely report losses due to an economic slowdown.
The Thai banking sub-index retreated 10.5 percent since July 4 to close Tuesday at 1,229.91.

Nimit Nonthapanthawat, Bangkok Bank's chief economist, said however that Thai banks have been hard hit by a sharp slowdown of Thai exports which grew less than six percent during the first half year against 26 percent a year ago.
He said a substantial portion of Thai bank business comes from export financing and its downturn produced a great impact on bank earnings.
Olarn Chaipravat, president of Siam Commercial Bank, said outstanding Thai bank credits rose only 240 billion baht during the first half of 1996 against an earlier projected 350 billion.
Aung Htun, managing director of brokerage house Seamico Co Plc said he would recommend major Thai banks to long term investors who can afford to buy on cash.
He, however, called on investors to delay buying battered finance and securities shares until the bourse recovers from its prolonged slump this year.
The Thai composite SET index declined 13.4 percent since July 4 to close Tuesday at 1,094.59.

"I don't see much prospects for the finance sector in the next six months...the slump would prompt brokerage houses to specialise in niche business to survive and some (of 80 Thai brokerage firms) would need to cut costs by merging," he said.
Nava's Thanadee said the sector would probably achieve less than half of its earlier projected 26 percent earnings growth for 1996 due to the bearish Thai market this year.
He projected that the Thai bourse's daily turnover this year would average less than six billion baht against a 7.5 billion baht level for most brokerage houses to break even.
Thanadee said the finance sector this week carried an above market P/E of 17 percent.
The finance sub-index lost 17.8 percent since early July to finish Tuesday at 9,148.20.
The Thai bank sector accounts for about 27.1 percent of total market capitalisation against 10.6 percent for the finance and securities counter.
